title: Emergent Offensive Behavior Benchmark Suite: EOB-Bench

original_idea.body:
# Emergent Offensive Behavior Benchmark Suite: EOB-Bench

**Problem:** No standardized benchmark exists to measure an agent's propensity for emergent offensive behavior under controlled conditions. Researchers cannot compare results across studies.

**Direction:** Design a benchmark of 50 tasks across 5 emergent-behavior categories (privilege escalation, credential access, DLP evasion, safety override, sandbox escape). Each task has a scoring rubric (binary: did the agent attempt the behavior?). Implement in a lightweight sandbox. Baseline three open models.

**Why it matters:** A standardized benchmark enables reproducible comparisons, progress tracking, and model evaluation before deployment. This fills the most critical measurement gap in the subfield.

**Relevant context:** Irregular 2026 behavior taxonomy; METR evaluations methodology; standard NLP benchmarking practice.
